sources.title: J. S. A. Elisonas, The Polity of the Tokugawa Era, Japan Society
sources.note: Full indexed original scholarly essay read; direct linked older route failed. Founding 1603, hereditary government through 1868, bakufu and domains, administrative samurai. Avoid its overbroad assertion that no noteworthy military conflict occurred between 1638 and 1863, which excludes Ainu resistance.

sources.title: Princeton University Art Museum, Japan Timeline, Edo period
sources.note: Direct Edo section read. Used only for Kyoto/Edo distinction and alternate attendance. Do not repeat inaccurate blanket Nagasaki-only foreign-contact statement, Meiji accession date, abolition chronology or 1856 treaty claim.

sources.title: Laws of Military Households, 1615, translated in David J. Lu, Japan: A Documentary History; Columbia Asia for Educators
sources.note: Direct two-page primary-source translation read. Articles 1, 6, 8 and 10 on studies, castles, marriage and dress. Rules express official intentions; not proof of universal obedience. No substantial direct quotation used.

sources.title: Ainu Association of Hokkaido, History of the Ainu
sources.note: Indexed original community chronology read. 1604 Matsumae trade monopoly, 1669 resistance, 1720 commercial subcontracting, 1799/1807 changes to direct shogunal government. Source does not validate imported northern islands as uniform sovereignty.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Dutch Factory on Deshima
sources.note: Direct original exhibit read. Dutch trading station moved 1641, restricted movement, exports and interpreters. Does not imply all foreign trade occurred through Dutch merchants.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Boom in Dutch Studies
sources.note: Direct original exhibit read. 1720 relaxation of non-Christian book ban, interpreters and scholars, family transmission in Sugita/Katsuragawa/Udagawa households.

sources.title: Edo-Tokyo Museum, Permanent Exhibition
sources.note: Direct institutional research-based exhibition account read. E2 row house reconstructions and bell records; E9 kabuki effects; E10 1868 transition. Avoid internally inconsistent area conversions for row houses. Exhibits are reconstructions, not surviving untouched homes.

sources.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks, Tamagawa Josui
sources.note: Direct Japanese original read. Construction began 1653; water supply in 1654. Open canal about 43 km Hamura to Yotsuya, 92 m height difference; underground wooden/stone pipes into southwestern Edo. No modern water-quality claim.

sources.title: Japan Ministry of the Environment, Night Soil Treatment and Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Systems in Japan, 2019
sources.note: Direct official PDF read. Printed page 2/human PDF page 2, Edo-era night soil storage and exchange for cash or vegetables. Page 3 discusses later sanitary treatment and pathogen control, not Edo achievement. No universal cleanliness or safe fertilizer claim.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Famous Places, People, and Social Customs on Paper: Sugoroku Board Games, 3rd Move
sources.note: Direct original exhibit read. Hiroshige calligraphy-school game, curriculum by occupation/gender, and food-market game. Same exhibit reproduced in NDL Newsletter 237 (March 2021), page 5, dates school print between 1843 and 1847; duplicate work treated together. Games are representations, not statistical surveys of all children.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Enthusiastic Eyes on Nature: The Eighteenth Century
sources.note: Direct original exhibit read. Uemura Masakatsu journals describing herb-gathering journeys 1720 to 1753, 140 to 190 days a year; shogunal agents also taught local people. Surviving copy transcribed in 1910, original work dated 1753. No claim that remedies were clinically effective.

sources.title: Institute of Science Tokyo Library, Kaitai Shinsho
sources.note: Direct institutional object description read. 1774, translators Sugita Genpaku/Maeno Ryotaku and others, illustrator Odano Naotake, four text volumes plus illustration volume, Dutch source based on Kulmus. English title New Book of Anatomy. Avoid unsupported broad claim that Japan previously lacked professional anatomy.

sources.title: Tohoku University Medical Library, 解體新書 巻之二, record 11990000040003
sources.note: Direct original holding catalogue read: exact traditional-character title 解體新書, reading カイタイ シンショ / Kaitai shinsho, Sugita Genpaku and 1774 date. Short sample is catalogue transcription, not independent decipherment of scan. English translation from Science Tokyo companion source.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Woodblock Prints in the Ukiyo-e Style
sources.note: Direct essay read. 1765 full-color calendar commissions; four contributors, designer/engraver/printer/publisher; printmaking process. Normalized English URL used, same work as localized /it/ version.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Opening of the Country: Dawn of the Modern Era
sources.note: Direct archive exhibit read. Perry 1853 visit, 1854 peace/amity treaty negotiations, Shimoda and Hakodate; formal ratification exchange 1855. Do not confuse 1854 agreement with 1858 commercial treaty.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Tokugawa Yoshinobu biography
sources.note: Direct institutional biography read. 1866 shogun, 1867 restoration of political power to emperor, failed attempt to preserve family power, defeat/confinement, later life. 1868 transition date separately supported by museum.

proposedOverrides.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
proposedOverrides.summary: Military government and regional domains sustained a changing society of towns, trade, scholarship and unequal status.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact uncovered record; map 1650 to 1783, historical government 1603 to 1868. Decoded 1650/1700 bounds [129.344,30.888,145.447,45.436], 1715 [129.344,30.888,150.498,46.215]. Broad northern Hokkaido/Kuril painting not accepted as uniform direct rule; community historical account distinguishes Matsumae trade monopoly and later government. No aliases attached. Existing Nara, Heian and Imperial Japan cards are chronologically distinct. Missing japan-1783 spans both late shogunate and Meiji and is not a simple alias; missing japan/japan-warring-states also left separate. Periods include full historical contextual sequence while override dates remain map coverage.
